rationale:
Repair of trial-af78dd3283 (the CUDA-graph replay of the phase-guarded Qwen3ForCausalLM prefill call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a), which was rejected for quality only: per-step logits max abs error 5.0625, 41.5% mismatched elements, on both continuous steps, while installation, direct module binding at the region root, coverage (root invoked 2/2) and routing all passed. The previous-feedback supplemental evidence names the measured mechanism: capturing the unchanged parent flips Transformers' tracing probe, because transformers.utils.import_utils.is_tracing() includes is_cuda_stream_capturing() (torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing(), transformers 5.16.1, import_utils.py:1776-1797). During stream capture it returns True, so masking_utils._ignore_causal_mask_sdpa returns False (masking_utils.py:259-260), a boolean 4D mask is materialized, and sdpa_attention_forward then sees attention_mask is not None: use_gqa_in_sdpa becomes False, K/V are repeat_kv-expanded to [1,32,256,128] and SDPA runs with is_causal=False plus the bool mask. The eager parent runs mask=None, GQA enabled, is_causal=True. The first attention output differs by 0.0009765625 and this compounds through the 36 layers to 5.0625 in the logits. The same record validates the repair direction: a diagnostic that preserved the eager attention decision during capture executed the graph with zero error over two complete generations.

This attempt keeps the previously validated machinery (boundary, signature guard on kwargs input_ids=[1,256] int64 CUDA / use_cache=True / logits_to_keep=1 with all optional inputs None, fresh DynamicCache snapshot viewing the graph-owned static K/V buffers, distinct fallback labels for unsupported signature, setup failure and runtime failure, lazy capture inside the first real adapter invocation with the evaluator's dispatch modes and the adapter's prefill phase active per inputs/binding-contract.md) and adds two things.
(1) Eager-decision-preserving capture: the graph-capture window only is wrapped in a temporary, try/finally-restored rebinding of transformers.utils.import_utils.is_cuda_stream_capturing to a constant False. No dynamo or jit tracing is active in this workload, so eager is_tracing() is False; the rebinding makes every capture-time Python decision of the parent (mask skip, GQA, causal flag) identical to the eager parent's decision for this exact call. This is not a global mask-policy change: outside the capture window the original probe is restored, decode and any other call never observe the patch, and padded inputs keep their normal semantics (the guard requires attention_mask=None anyway). If the probe cannot be resolved in a future layout, an is_tracing-level fallback is used; if that also fails, capture runs unpatched and the verification gate decides.
(2) A bit-exactness gate at setup: right after capture, the engine replays the graph and compares with torch.equal the replayed [1,1,151936] bf16 logits and layer-0 K/V ([1,8,256,128] bf16) against a fresh, unpatched eager run of the same parent callable on the live input_ids. Replay of the identical captured kernel sequence on the same pointers must be bit-identical to the eager parent (the diagnostic observed zero error over two complete generations); any mismatch raises, permanently disables the graph and the parent serves every subsequent call. The accepted graph path therefore reproduces parent quality by construction, and a silent numerics regression is impossible without an explicit fallback.

Steady-state effect hypothesis (to be tested by the bound worker, not a claim): replaying the region as a single graph launch removes most of the per-launch host dispatch bubbles between the region's 2145 recorded kernels (21.72 ms inclusive diagnostic CUDA time for the region root in target-resources.json) against the 27.681 ms clean original ttft baseline, so ttft_ms should approach the ~22-23 ms GPU execution floor while the 31 eager decode steps, the frozen workload, sampling semantics and all quality checks stay untouched. The boundary is the selected region only: mixed-phase groups (argmax, select, unsqueeze, to.dtype, expand) and the adapter-level logits slice and first argmax remain on the parent path, as in the accepted selection.
setup_work: All setup is lazy and one-time, inside the first real adapter invocation (a warmup invocation; the framework's warmup=2 absorbs it), with the evaluator's dispatch modes and the adapter's prefill phase active: (a) copy the live input_ids into a static [1,256] int64 buffer; (b) three eager warmup forwards of the unmodified parent callable on a side stream plus a synchronize (CUDA-graph recipe; results discarded); (c) one unpatched eager reference forward on the live input for the verification gate (its DynamicCache discarded); (d) capture of the parent callable into one torch.cuda.CUDAGraph, with transformers' is_cuda_stream_capturing probe temporarily rebound to False so capture-time decisions match the eager parent (try/finally restore); (e) one verification replay plus torch.equal comparisons and one synchronize. No model weights or parameters are transformed; no fixture outputs are cached (every invocation copies the current input_ids and replays). Memory: the graph retains a private CUDA memory pool holding the static input buffer (~2 KB), the static [1,1,151936] bf16 logits (~0.3 MB), the 72 static K/V buffers (36 layers x 2 x [1,8,256,128] bf16, ~37.7 MB), and the capture-time activation blocks; expect framework.lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes and retained pool bytes to increase, while warm-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes can fall because prefill intermediates are allocated inside the graph pool instead of the regular allocator - a counter effect, not a physical-memory saving. Setup failures, unresolved patch points or verification mismatch keep the parent on every call.
quality_risks: Graph capture could still diverge from eager execution through an unobserved capture-sensitive decision; mitigated by the scoped eager-decision patch and made non-observable by the torch.equal verification gate (any mismatch permanently reverts to the parent before the first replay result is returned).
Kernel-level nondeterminism between the captured sequence and the eager reference would fail the bit-exact gate and cost the speedup (parent fallback), never quality.

Replay does not rerun Python hooks, so the region's inner calls are not individually observable during replay; coverage of the selected root replacement and the returned region outputs (logits + KV consumed unchanged by the eager decode loop) remain the evidence, as in the previously passed coverage run.

The graph-owned static K/V buffers are read-only inputs to DynamicLayer.update's torch.cat reassignment (no in-place writes), so decode cannot corrupt them; per-invocation fresh cache containers prevent cross-invocation aliasing.

If a later invocation arrives with a different signature, the guard routes it to the parent (prefill_parent_signature_fallback); decode-phase calls are outside this replacement and never see the patch, which is active only inside the capture context manager.
Any runtime replay error disables the graph and falls back to the parent for the current and all later invocations (prefill_parent_runtime_fallback).
